source_notes.label: Three charges create three named composites
source_notes.summary: SnCl2·2H2O charges of 300, 600 and 1200 mg are paired with the same 100 mL aqueous GO input at 0.2 g/L. The products are SnO2/G-0.3, -0.6 and -1.2, respectively. All are stirred for 24 h at room temperature, collected, washed and dried at 100 °C. The GO preparation is cited rather than reproduced; this recipe starts from the supplied GO dispersion.

source_notes.label: Coupled redox is the authors’ interpretation
source_notes.summary: The authors interpret the process as Sn2+ oxidation coupled to GO deoxygenation, supported by SnO2 diffraction and changes in FTIR/XPS. The proposed transformation is not a balanced experimentally measured reaction equation. No unique oxygen content of GO or graphene, tin conversion yield or dissolved speciation is supplied.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 1–3, Preparation and structural/spectroscopic discussion

source_notes.label: Size and structure describe different quantities
source_notes.summary: XRD gives tetragonal SnO2 and Scherrer domain sizes of 8.4, 7.8 and 8.4 nm for the three composites. The text’s less-than-10 nm TEM statement is scoped to SnO2/G-0.3. Figure 3 annotates d(110) = 0.34 nm in each sample panel. The predicted Bragg value 0.337 nm is reference interpretation, not a second measured lattice spacing. No unit-cell refinement or coordinates are supplied.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figures 1–3 and results

source_notes.label: More tin changes loading and morphology
source_notes.summary: TGA gives approximate SnO2 mass percentages of 63, 68 and 74%. The source attributes the slower increase in SnO2 fraction than tin charge to partial SnCl2 loss, without measuring a recovery balance. TEM indicates more oxide particles on smaller graphene sheets as tin charge increases; numerical sheet dimensions are unreported.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2–3, Morphology and TGA discussion

source_notes.label: Spectral comparisons retain their scope
source_notes.summary: GO bands are assigned at 1401, 1735, 1220, 1052, 827 and 1620 cm−1. The source assigns the composite-series 606 cm−1 band to Sn–O and interprets loss of several oxygen-group bands as reduction. GO Raman G and D positions are 1591.3 and 1365.6 cm−1; composite D/G ratios are 1.13, 1.25 and 1.34. These ratios are not particle sizes. XPS binding energies are scoped to GO or the SnO2/G-0.3 comparison as stated.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2–3, FTIR, Raman and XPS discussion

source_notes.label: Electrode processing is a separate supporting route
source_notes.summary: Each composite is mixed with carbon black and PVDF at 80:15:5 by weight in NMP, doctor-bladed onto copper and vacuum-dried at 120 °C for 8 h. Cells use lithium foil, polypropylene separator and 1 M LiPF6 in EC/DMC (1:1 by weight), with overnight soaking. These steps support the electrochemical measurements and do not demonstrate new nanoparticle structures.

source_notes.label: Battery results are specimen-linked
source_notes.summary: At 200 mA/g between 0.01 and 1.5 V versus Li, reported reversible capacities are 541.3, 402.7 and 222.4 mAh/g. After 35 cycles, retentions are about 69.7, 34.2 and 33.6%; only the 0.3 specimen has a separately stated 35-cycle capacity, 377.3 mAh/g. The authors propose that larger graphene sheets and lower oxide coverage reduce pulverization and improve conduction. These mechanisms are interpretations, not directly measured stress or conductivity.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 4, Figure 7 and discussion

source_notes.label: References and introductory values are not new product data
source_notes.summary: The introductory 782 mAh/g theoretical SnO2 capacity, literature bare-SnO2 performance and prospective sensor uses are background. No standalone pure SnO2 comparator synthesis is given here. All 33 bibliography entries are retained, but their full sources are unreviewed.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 1, 4–5, Introduction, conclusion and bibliography

evidence_conflicts: Main p. 2 cites Figure 2a/2b for the 0.3 specimen TEM discussion; the 0.34 nm annotations themselves appear in Figure 3a–c. Figure locators and sample assignments are kept distinct.
Main p. 2 refers to Figure 6 for the Sn 3d doublet, while the actual doublet appears in Figure 5B; Figure 6 is TGA.
Figure 3d labels the horizontal axis Wavelength (cm−1). Printed axis text is retained; wavenumber-valued FTIR positions are reported without altering the source image.
Main uses both graphite oxide and graphene oxide (GO); source wording is retained without assigning a unique oxygen stoichiometry or treating them as distinct measured batches.

The source prose calls the 0.3 sample size less than 10 nm; the three XRD domain sizes and Figure 3 fringe labels are separately sample-resolved. The size bound is not copied to the other two samples.
